questions.q: Where did Boaz go to resolve the issue of who would be the kinsman-redeemer for Ruth?
questions.a: He went to the gate of the city.

questions.q: Who did Boaz ask to sit as witnesses?
questions.a: He asked ten men who were from the elders of the city.

questions.q: What did Boaz first speak about to the other kinsman?
questions.a: He told him that Naomi was selling the piece of land that had been owned by Elimelek.

questions.q: What did Boaz suggest the other kinsman do about the parcel of land?
questions.a: Boaz suggested that the other kinsman could redeem it.

questions.q: What was the other kinsman’s answer?
questions.a: He said he would redeem it.

questions.q: About what additional requirement did Boaz then tell the other kinsman?
questions.a: He told him that he would also have to marry Ruth in order to raise up the name of the dead man over his inheritance.

questions.q: What was the other kinsman’s answer when he learned that he would have to marry Ruth?
questions.a: He said he could not redeem the land.

questions.q: Why did the other kinsman say he could not be the redeemer?
questions.a: He said that it would damage his own inheritance.

questions.q: What did the other kinsman do to show that he agreed that Boaz should be the redeemer?
questions.a: He took off his sandal and gave it to him in front of witnesses.

questions.q: What was the first agreement that Boaz said the elders witnessed?
questions.a: They witnessed that Boaz bought all the land that had belonged to Elimelek.

questions.q: What was the second agreement that Boaz said the elders had witnessed?
questions.a: They had witnessed that Boaz acquired Ruth as his wife.

questions.q: What blessing did the people desire for Boaz?
questions.a: They desired that Yahweh would give him offspring through Ruth, just as Tamar bore a son to Judah.

questions.q: Why did the women say that Ruth was better for Naomi than seven sons?
questions.a: They said this because of Ruth’s love for Naomi, and because Ruth had given birth to a grandson for Naomi.

questions.q: What was Naomi’s relationship with Ruth’s son?
questions.a: Naomi became his nurse or caregiver.

questions.q: Of whom was Obed the father and grandfather?
questions.a: Obed was the father of Jesse and the grandfather of David.

commentary.text: The kinsman refuses to redeem Ruth's inheritance.

Verses 1–8 This matter depended on the laws given by Moses about inheritances, and doubtless the whole was settled in the regular and legal manner. This kinsman, when he heard the conditions of the bargain, refused it. In like manner many are shy of the great redemption; they are not willing to espouse religion; they have heard well of it, and have nothing to say against it; they will give it their good word, but they are willing to part with it, and cannot be bound to it, for fear of marring their own inheritance in this world. The right was resigned to Boaz. Fair and open dealing in all matters of contract and trade, is what all must make conscience of, who would approve themselves true Israelites, without guile. Honesty will be found the best policy.

Men are ready to seize opportunities for increasing their estates, but few know the value of godliness. Such are the wise men of this world, whom the Lord charges with folly. They attend not to the concerns of their souls, but reject the salvation of Christ, for fear of marring their inheritance. But God did Boaz the honour to bring him into the line of the Messiah, while the kinsman, who was afraid of lessening himself, and marring his inheritance, has his name, family, and inheritance forgotten.

Ruth bore a son, through whom thousands and myriads were born to God; and in being the lineal ancestor of Christ, she was instrumental in the happiness of all that shall be saved by him; even of us Gentiles, as well as those of Jewish descent. She was a witness for God to the Gentile world, that he had not utterly forsaken them, but that in due time they should become one with his chosen people, and partake of his salvation. Prayer to God attended the marriage, and praise to him attended the birth of the child. What a pity it is that pious language should not be more used among Christians, or that it should be let fall into formality! Here is the descent of David from Ruth. And the period came when Bethlehem-Judah displayed greater wonders than those in the history of Ruth, when the outcast babe of another forlorn female of the same race appeared, controlling the counsels of the Roman master of the world, and drawing princes and wise men from the east, with treasures of gold, and frankincense, and myrrh to his feet. His name shall endure for ever, and all nations shall call Him blessed. In that Seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed.
